text:
maya: Heads-up — proposal to add a small "priority band" field to rerank requests so routing + prefetch can treat urgent traffic differently. low friction change on the API side, big ops/console UX implications.

sam: curious — what does "priority band" map to? model selection, tenant quota, or just queue priority?

maya: all of the above ideally. band: {gold, silver, bronze}. Routing policy would prefer lower-latency model variants for gold, allow higher fanout for silver, and apply tighter candidate caps for bronze. also toggles whether KV-prefetch is allowed.

lee: prefer enums over free text. also need deterministic fallback when gold capacity exhausted — do we downgrade to silver or backoff?

maya: downgrade to silver by default, with explicit "no-fallback" flag if a caller wants hard failure. fallback policy would be a tenant-configurable rollout knob in the console.

diego: telemetry ask: need counters for "band_requested", "band_served", "band_fallback_reason" and histogram for latency by band+model_variant. otherwise we can't measure cost/benefit.

ops-bot: ACTION logged: create telemetry ticket with those metrics (TICKET-879).

sam: quota model question — do we charge same score-units across bands? If gold allows higher fanout and lower local candidate-thresholds we could blow budgets.

maya: proposal: bill tokens/score-units as usual, but console shows an estimated cost multiplier for each band (e.g., gold x1.6, silver x1.0, bronze x0.7). That keeps billing simple but surfaces economics.

lee: console UX — we need a per-route override and a global default. For rollouts, a canary toggle that only sends X% of gold requests to new model_variant. Also show a small chart: requests by band over time + average cost.

console-ui: can implement per-route band defaults + canary slider. question: what's the shape of the API field? simplest: `priority_band: "gold"` plus optional `no_fallback: true` and optional `model_hint: "gptx-rerank-v2"`.

maya: yep exactly. sample body:```json
{
  "candidates": [...],
  "priority_band": "gold",
  "no_fallback": false,
  "model_hint": "rdr-rank-small-v1"
}
```

sam: security/compliance note — bronze should never allow KV-prefetch for tenants with PII flags. Need an enforcement hook in the routing policy.

diego: telemetry follow-up: also capture model_hint accepted vs ignored counts. add a label for fallback path: capacity / model_incompatible / quota.

maya: ops question — how do we surface soft-quota throttles? If gold hits its reserved GPU pool, do we return HTTP 429 with `retry_after` or return a 200 with `partial_scores` and a `fallback_notice` field?

lee: prefer explicit 429 for strict SLAs. For best-effort bronze/silver return partial + notice. But we need a consistent client contract.

maya: agreed. update spec: band+tenant policy determines error mode. Default: gold -> 429 on insufficient reserved capacity; silver -> best-effort partial; bronze -> best-effort or reject depending on tenant flag.

sam: implementation note — routing layer needs quick checks for reserved capacity per band per region. Caching these as a small in-memory sharded table should keep latency low.

console-ui: will add a dashboard card: band distribution, avg-latency per band, cost-multiplier estimate, fallback rate. Also add a rollout panel that shows which tenants have overrides.

diego: recommend adding a sampling trace for 1% of requests that includes full fanout list + decision path for postmortems.

maya: +1. final items: create API spec PR, add telemetry ticket, add console mockups, and an ops runbook for gold 429 scenarios. I'll open the PRs.

ops-bot: ACTION logged: API spec PR (PR-2048), telemetry ticket (TICKET-879), console mockup task (UI-442), runbook (RUN-77).

sam: thanks — please @me on the PRs, I can review routing logic and quota calc.

maya: will do. :thumbsup:
